title: Make a moka pot ready to brew: water to just below the safety valve, the coffee basket in, the top screwed on snug
instruction: Get the moka pot ready to brew.
context: A stovetop moka pot is one of the most familiar ways to make coffee at home, and every one is put together the same way at the counter before it goes on the stove: fill the base with water up to just below the brass safety valve, never over it, set the funnel basket of ground coffee in, then hold the base and screw the upper chamber on, straight, until the gasket is snug. Over the valve, the valve stands in water and cannot vent steam if the coffee clogs the funnel; more than about 1 cm under it makes weak coffee; a top that is loose, or started crooked so it cross-threads, leaks steam and hot coffee at the gasket. Water poured onto the basket runs over the grounds and off the rim. Emptying the carafe in, leaving the basket out, or forcing a crooked top are the tempting wrong answers.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, table (counter) top z = 0, all at real size. The empty base (water chamber) of a 3-cup cast-aluminum moka pot (Bialetti Moka Express 3-cup or similar) stands free on the counter, axis at (27, 5): not clamped, 0.30 kg (estimate), 7.2 cm tall, octagonal outside (8.0 cm across the flats, flats facing the x and y axes) up to a threaded collar 6.6 cm across (its top 1.2 cm). The collar carries the male thread: 66 mm major diameter, single start, right hand, 3.0 mm pitch, 1.2 mm deep, 1.5 turns, its top 5 mm under the rim. Inside, the base steps from 7.2 to 6.6 to 6.2 cm across, floor 4 mm above the foot, steps 2.4 and 4.4 cm above the foot. Its brass safety valve (hex 1.3 cm across, with a pin) faces the robot (-x), its center 5.0 cm above the foot; the valve's 8 mm bore shows as a brass ring inside the wall, its bottom edge 4.6 cm above the foot (155.8 mL of water). The upper chamber (aluminum, 200 g, free) stands upright on the counter at (24, 19): 8.7 cm tall, 7.0 cm across on its lower body and 8.0 cm at the top, with a lid knob, a small spout and a black plastic handle pointing 45 degrees off the x axis, and a skirt 1.2 cm deep under it carrying the female thread (same pitch, 1.5 turns, 0.3 mm flank clearance) and, under its bottom face, a rubber gasket ring 5.2 to 6.2 cm across. A glass carafe (cylinder 4.9 cm across, 13.5 cm tall, 4.4 cm inside, 200 g) holding 175 mL of water stands at (23, -12). The funnel basket (stainless steel, free, 40 g with its coffee) is filled level with 15 g of ground coffee: a flange 6.12 cm across and 1.5 mm thick, a cup 6.1 cm across tapering to 4.6 cm at its perforated floor 2.0 cm down, and a stem 1.0 cm across and 3.8 cm long. It stands in a white ceramic espresso cup (5.4 cm across, 5.0 cm tall, 4.2 cm across inside its mouth, fixed) at (36, -7), its floor on the cup's rim and its stem inside, as it is set down after being filled. In the base the basket drops into the mouth (its cup a close fit in the bore) and hangs by its flange on the rim, its stem ending 1 cm above the floor, and the upper chamber's gasket presses down on the flange; assembled the pot is 16 cm tall. No stove is in the scene: the pot goes on it after this task. The water is drawn as a blue column inside each vessel.
scoring: The trial scores 1.0 when, at the end, the base holds 122.5 to 155.8 mL, the basket is in it with its coffee, the upper chamber is screwed on snug over it, no more than 5 mL is spilled, the carafe stands upright and let go, the base stands upright, and no gripper is touching the pot; where the arms end up is not scored. It scores 0.75 when the pot is ready but over 5 mL is spilled, the carafe is still held or tipped, the base is tipped over 10 degrees, or a gripper still touches the upper chamber or the base (the pot has not been let go). It scores 0.5 when the water and basket are right but the upper chamber is not screwed snug: left off, set on but not screwed down, put on before the basket, or cross-threaded. Snug means threaded on straight (its bottom face within 4 mm of the rim height, its axis within 2 mm and 1.5 degrees of the base's; the thread's 0.3 mm flank clearance allows about 1 degree, one groove off is 2.6 degrees) and the gasket pressed at least 0.10 mm onto the basket's flange: the about 52 N that 2.5 N·m of screwing torque clamps through the modeled thread, over the gasket's estimated 5e5 N/m. 2.5 N·m is firm hand-tight for a 65 mm closure, from published closure and jar-torque data (see README). A top started crooked rides on the crests or binds one groove off and never gets there, whatever the torque. It scores 0.25 when the water is right but the basket is not in with its coffee (flange within 2 mm of the rim, axis within 4 mm and 5 degrees of the base's; tipped past 45 degrees for two control steps on the way, the grounds fell out), or when 30 to 122.5 mL went in (more than 1 cm under the valve: weak coffee) and the pot is otherwise ready. Otherwise it scores 0; doing nothing scores 0. It is 0 with more than 155.8 mL in the base (water above the bottom of the safety valve's bore, so the valve could not vent steam if the funnel clogs), under 30 mL, or 30 to 122.5 mL without a ready pot. Water poured while the basket is in or just over the mouth lands on the grounds and runs off the rim, so it counts as spilled. The screwing only counts if the basket was already in when the upper chamber went on. Touching means the gripper's own shape (palm and both fingers at their present opening) in contact with the part, within 2 mm; this is a release check. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. A real trial weighs the water in the base before the basket goes in, photographs the basket in the base from above before the top goes on, and checks snug with a torque reading: after the robot lets go, a jar-torque gauge or a strap wrench with a luggage scale at a known radius turns the top further clockwise; it is snug if it does not move below 2.5 N·m, and cross-threaded if it sits crooked or binds short of the gasket. A towel under the pot is weighed for spills.
reset_notes: Empty and dry the base and stand it free on the counter at (27, 5) with the valve toward the robot; unscrew the upper chamber and stand it upright at (24, 19) with its handle 45 degrees off the x axis; refill the funnel basket level with 15 g of ground coffee and stand it in the espresso cup at (36, -7); refill the carafe to 175 mL with a measuring jug and stand it at (23, -12); replace the towel under the pot.
fidelity: Real size. Water: a deterministic flow model; coffee: not particles, lost if the basket tips past 45 degrees. The thread is collider boxes along a helix (pitch and turns estimated, not measured); the gasket is a compliant contact ring, its stiffness estimated and set in the sim. The base is free, steadied only by the demo's other hand. Basket and base mouth: metal friction 0.6/0.47 (steel on aluminum); thread 1.1/1.0 (aluminum). No heat or steam.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (4,000 steps, hit the step limit); demo: 1.0 (2,583 steps)
